skill.name: git-operation
skill.description: Guides basic Git commit preparation with clear English commit messages and project checks.
skill.summary: Use a simple checklist for clean Git commits.
skill.author: 5t111111

security_audit.summary: The two static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline command formatting in SKILL.md. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or executable code was found in the reviewed skill content.

static_findings.snippet: - Always run `mise run fmt` to format the code before committing
- Always run `mise run test` before committing code changes to ensure no tests

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 18 contains a Markdown inline command example, not executable Ruby or shell code. It instructs users to run a project formatter before committing and does not accept user input.
Line 19 contains a Markdown inline command example, not executable Ruby or shell code. It instructs users to run tests before committing and does not create a command injection path.

content.value_statement: Teams need consistent commit hygiene and basic Git checks. This skill guides concise English commit messages and required format and test commands.
actual_capabilities: Guides English Git commit message writing.
Prompts concise first-line summaries for commits.
Explains when to add a blank line and bullet details.
Reminds users to run the project formatter before committing.
Reminds users to run the project test command before committing.
limitations: It does not perform Git commits by itself.
It assumes the project uses mise tasks named fmt and test.
It does not define branch, merge, or release workflows.
It does not validate command output unless the user provides it.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Clean Commit
use_cases.description: Follow a short checklist before creating a commit in a project repository.

use_cases.title: Standardize Commit Messages
use_cases.description: Keep commit messages concise, English, and easy for teammates to review.

use_cases.title: Review Changes Before Submission
use_cases.description: Check that formatting and tests have been run before opening a review request.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Commit Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me write a concise English Git commit message for these changes: [describe changes].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Commit Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through the required steps before I commit my current changes in this repository.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Draft Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Git commit message and make it clearer while keeping the first line concise: [paste message].

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Detailed Commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a commit message with a concise first line and bullet details for this multi-part change: [describe changes].

output_examples.input: I changed Figma variable export naming and updated related documentation.
output_examples.output:
Update variable export naming

- Clarify generated token names
- Refresh related documentation

output_examples.input: I need a pre-commit checklist for a small code change.
output: Review the changed files for unrelated edits.
Write a concise English commit message.

output_examples.input: My draft message says fixed stuff. Improve it.
output_examples.output:
Fix theme variable generation

- Correct generated variable names
- Update tests for the new behavior

best_practices: Keep the first commit message line short and specific.
Run formatting and tests before creating the commit.
Use bullet details only when the change needs more context.
anti_patterns: Do not commit with vague messages such as fixed stuff.
Do not skip project checks before committing code changes.
Do not mix unrelated changes into one commit message.

faq.question: Does this skill run Git commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance for commit preparation and message writing.

faq.question: What language should commit messages use?
faq.answer: Commit messages should be written in English.

faq.question: When should I add bullet details?
faq.answer: Add them when the first line needs supporting details or context.

faq.question: Does this skill require mise?
faq.answer: The documented checks use mise commands, so it fits projects that define those tasks.

faq.question: Can it help rewrite a weak commit message?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the draft message and describe the change you made.

faq.question: Is this only for Claude?
faq.answer: No. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
